summary: One headline number, with just enough around it to say what it is and whether it is a problem.

pairs.dont: Put two or three numbers in one tile.
pairs.do: One number per tile, or use a Card if they belong together.
pairs.why: The tile's whole layout is built to make one figure the loudest thing on it. A second number halves that and neither reads at a glance.

pairs.dont: Label a tile "MOS" and leave the reader to work out whose.
pairs.do: Name the measure and its scope — "Network MOS", "Endpoints online".
pairs.why: A dashboard is read in one pass. A label that needs the surrounding page to make sense fails the moment the tile is seen on its own.

pairs.dont: Set a status on a tile nobody would act on.
pairs.do: Use status where there is a threshold and a response.
pairs.why: A status badge is a claim that something needs attention. On a number that is merely interesting it trains people to ignore the badge everywhere.

pairs.do: Put "4.0" in the value and "/ 5" in the unit.
pairs.why: The value is set in the metric face at 30px and the unit in body at 14px. Rolling them together makes the qualifier as loud as the figure.

pairs.dont: Show 0 when a probe has stopped reporting.
pairs.do: Use status unknown and an em dash for the value.
pairs.why: Zero is a measurement. A tile showing 0 for a dead probe is stating something false, and someone will act on it.

pairs.dont: Mix tile widths, or drop one tile into a page on its own.
pairs.do: Use them in a row or grid of peers, at equal width.
pairs.why: The quiet border and missing shadow are tuned for a set. A single tile on a page reads as an unfinished card.

a11y: The meter is aria-hidden decoration. The number and the status badge are the accessible content — which is why the badge's word is not optional, and why status never relies on the meter's colour alone.
The label is a <div>, not a heading. A grid of tiles that should appear in the page outline needs headings supplied around them.
